title: The Thief and the Shroff
logline: A cocky thief steals a money-changer's purse to win a dare, learns an innocent maid is being punished for it, and pulls a second, cleverer trick that clears her while he still keeps the gold.
moral: A clever deed is not finished while an innocent person pays for it.
tone: Light-footed caper comedy with one real pang of conscience; the punishment is threatened, never shown landing.

beats.summary: The shroff walks the market with a purse full of gold.
A gang of thieves sees the purse.
One boasts he can take it alone; the others laugh and dare him.
The purse goes onto a high shelf at home.
The maid goes for water and leaves the door open.
The thief takes the purse unseen.
He waits for praise that does not come.
His companions show him the cost: the maid will be blamed and beaten.
An innocent will pay instead of the thief; he decides to go back.
He finds the shroff punishing the maid.
He knocks and poses as a messenger returning a found purse.
The shroff reaches; the thief holds the purse back and demands a sealed receipt.
While the shroff writes, the thief runs off with the same purse.
The shroff loses his gold but stops punishing the maid.
The second trick succeeds and the maid is saved from unjust punishment.

subtitles.ar: مر صراف في السوق يحمل كيسًا مليئًا بالنقود الذهبية.|رآه جماعة من اللصوص،|فقال أحدهم بثقة إنه يستطيع أخذ الكيس وحده.|ضحك أصحابه، وطلبوا منه أن يريهم كيف يفعل ذلك.
subtitles.en: A money-changer passed through the market carrying gold coins.|A thief boasted to his companions|that he could steal the purse by himself,|and they challenged him to prove it.

subtitles.ar: تبع اللص الصراف من بعيد حتى وصل إلى بيته.|دخل الصراف، ووضع الكيس على رف مرتفع،|ثم ذهب إلى الحمام. طلب من خادمته أن تحضر له إبريق ماء،|فتركت الباب مفتوحًا.
subtitles.en: The thief followed him home.|The money-changer put the purse on a high shelf,|then went to the lavatory, asking his maid to bring water.|She left the door open.

subtitles.ar: تسلل اللص إلى البيت، وأخذ الكيس من الرف،|وخرج سريعًا دون أن يراه أحد.|رجع إلى أصحابه فرحًا، ووضع المال أمامهم،|وهو ينتظر أن يمدحوا جرأته وسرعة حركته.
subtitles.en: The thief slipped inside, took the purse|and escaped unseen.|He returned proudly to his companions,|expecting them to praise his daring and speed.

subtitles.ar: لكن أحد اللصوص قال له إن الصراف سيكتشف ضياع المال،|ثم يتهم الخادمة ويضربها.|وقال آخر إن السرقة لم تكتمل بعد،|ما دام شخص بريء سيدفع ثمنها بدل اللص.
subtitles.en: Instead, his companions warned that the money-changer|would accuse and beat the innocent maid.|They said his trick was incomplete|unless he saved her from punishment.

subtitles.ar: عاد اللص إلى البيت، فوجد الصراف غاضبًا يعاقب الخادمة.|طرق الباب، وادعى أنه رسول من جار الصراف في السوق،|جاء ليعيد كيسًا وجده مرميًا قرب الدكان وحفظه من الضياع.
subtitles.en: He returned and found the maid being punished.|Knocking, he pretended to be a messenger from a neighboring shopkeeper|who had found and safeguarded the missing purse.

subtitles.ar: أخرج اللص الكيس وأراه للصراف،|فعرفه الرجل ومد يده ليأخذه.|لكن اللص قال إنه لا يستطيع تسليمه إلا بعد أن يكتب الصراف ورقة|تثبت وصول المال إليه، مختومة بختمه.
subtitles.en: The thief showed the familiar purse.|When the money-changer reached for it,|he demanded a signed, sealed receipt|to prove to his supposed employer that he had delivered it.

subtitles.ar: دخل الصراف ليكتب الورقة ويختمها،|وظن أن ماله قد عاد إليه.|وفي اللحظة التي ابتعد فيها،|ركض اللص خارج الباب ومعه الكيس نفسه، واختفى في شوارع المدينة المزدحمة.
subtitles.en: The money-changer went inside to write the receipt,|believing his money restored.|As soon as he turned away,|the thief ran off with the very same purse.

subtitles.ar: لم يسترد الصراف نقوده،|لكنه توقف عن معاقبة الخادمة، بعدما ظهر أن الكيس لم يختف بسبب تقصيرها.|أما اللص فقد نجح في خدعته الثانية،|ونجت الخادمة من العقوبة الظالمة.
subtitles.en: The money-changer did not recover his gold,|but the maid escaped further punishment.|The thief kept the purse|and saved her from the blame his first trick had caused.

new_assets.name: purse
new_assets.description: The planned fat coin purse with drawstring, coin mark, open, swing and ghost fields (see props).
new_assets.implementation: One function purse(ctx, x, y, {s, open, swing, sq, ghost}): body with shape() from an ellipse belly plus a pinched neck polygon, yellow fill with red dot shading; drawstring as two seg() strokes; coin rims as 3 to 5 yellow ellipses at the mouth; ghost draws the outline only with a dashed stroke. Rotate about the string end for swing.

new_assets.name: scroll (with quillInk)
new_assets.description: Planned scroll as a receipt with lines 0..3 and a red seal 0..1, plus the planned quill and inkpot.
new_assets.implementation: Paper polygon with two curled end ellipses; wavy lines with K.noise offsets, revealed by count; seal as a red disc with a star and impactSquash on arrival. Quill: a tapering white feather polygon on a black nib; inkpot: small navy trapezoid.

new_assets.name: waterJug
new_assets.description: Ewer 60 x 110 with spout, handle, fill and tilt.
new_assets.implementation: Ellipse belly, neck rectangle, spout triangle and a stroked loop handle, drawn with shape() in terracotta with red dots; blue ellipse at the mouth when fill > 0; rotate about the base for tilt.

new_assets.name: thief disguise turban
new_assets.description: The planned thief disguise overlay (KD-013), turban item only: a small white turban drawn over the cap of the thief kind, following head moves; also drawable as a loose prop.
new_assets.implementation: Opt-in field on person (disguise: 'turban') that draws the people.js turban shape at the thief head position after the cap; default off so the regression test stays identical. In the story first, as a scene overlay at the head point returned by the person pose.

new_assets.name: sneak
new_assets.description: The planned tiptoe option for walk(): high knees and a short hold on each toe.
new_assets.implementation: Wrap walk(): remap the leg phase with a stepped ease so each foot holds at the top for about 40 % of the step, raise amp, add 6 units of body lift on the hold; footfalls() still gives the toe taps.

new_assets.name: runInPlace
new_assets.description: The planned comic wind-up: legs cycle at run amplitude with no travel for about 0.3 s, dust building, then release.
new_assets.implementation: Drive ph from time (not distance) while x is held, amp 1.5, tip ramping to 0.2, dustBurst behind the heels every 3 frames; hand over to walk(TX, t) at the release time with matching phase.

new_assets.name: iconBalloon
new_assets.description: The planned wordless picture balloon (single mode): speech balloon with a tail to the speaker, content drawn by a callback and swappable with a pop.
new_assets.implementation: Rounded box via the style box primitive or shape() with a triangular tail; pop scale with overshoot; inside(ctx) callback clipped to the balloon; icons here: purse, waterJug, merchant head (person head clipped), marketStall at small scale, townDoor, scroll, quill, tick, seal.

new_assets.name: streetCrowd
new_assets.description: A flow of 8 to 10 passers-by built from the existing person costume presets, walking both ways in two depth rows so a character can vanish among them.
new_assets.implementation: streetCrowd(ctx, t, {x0, x1, n, seed, row}): for each i a seeded preset, pal override, scale, speed (40 to 90 units/s), direction and start phase; x from time modulo the span, legs from walk() on that x function so feet never slide; call once with row 'back' before the hero and once with row 'front' after him. No unique drawings.

new_assets.name: flush
new_assets.description: The planned anger flush: red dots climbing the face plus two steam puffs.
new_assets.implementation: Opt-in person field flush 0..1: a clipped red Ben-Day overlay on the face rising from the chin, and two small cloud puffs beside the head when above 0.8.

new_assets.name: coinPile
new_assets.description: The planned coin mound, used small (5 loose coins) when the purse opens on the crate and as stacks on the desk.
new_assets.implementation: Seeded yellow ellipses with a darker rim and a glint; n coins; kick() offset for the hop.

owner_questions: The punishment is never shown landing: the shroff shakes a raised stick and the maid kneels behind her hands (in the warning cloud and in P5); default: keep it softened this way.
The thief's messenger disguise is an invented small white turban jammed over his masked cap (not in the script); default: keep it as the visual joke and as the object the maid finds at the end.
The lavatory is shown only as a closed curtain alcove with the shroff's head and hand appearing at its edge; default: keep it discreet.
Added acting beyond the script: the thief hushes and winks at the maid before he runs (134.4) and she ends holding his turban with a knowing smile; default: keep, it ties her rescue to him.
The ending adds the companions applauding the second trick (BRAVO!, TRICK 2 counter) as the payoff of the praise he awaited in P3; default: keep.
Invented comic lettering (PURSE, ALONE!, SHOW US!, DOOR OPEN!, NOPE!, RECEIPT, THE SAME PURSE!, GONE!, GOLD: 0, NOT HER FAULT, BRAVO!) is English only; default: keep, about 30 words in the film.

The story lets the thief keep the stolen gold; the film plays the stated lesson (no innocent should pay) and gives the shroff a sulking, not tragic, ending; default: follow the script without an added judgement.
implementation_notes: Start from Library/template. Word cues: use w(p, n) from timing.json; every cue in this plan is the exact word start on the final MP3.

Sets are single calls that return anchors: const M = marketStreet(ctx, {...}); const H = palaceHall(ctx, {variant: 'merchant', ...}). Read door, shelf, desk and curtain positions from the anchors (MERCHANT constants with the lowered shelves option), not from this plan's rounded numbers.

Interior scale: people at s 1.45 to 1.5 (about 350 tall) so faces read on a phone; the top shelf is lowered to y 500 so a figure standing on the stool with raised arm angles reaches it. Check with a still at 29.9 and 46.6 and adjust the shelf y, not the arms.
Peeks and hiding: draw the actor, then redraw the occluder (door frame strip, stall front, barrel, crowd front row). No clipped second copies.

The purse is one prop instance with a holder state keyed over time (shroff sash, shelf, thief hand, crate, pal2 hand, thief behind back, thief hand running) so it never duplicates; the dashed ghost stays on the shelf from 47.44 to the end of the film.
Thought clouds use Library thoughtCloud with inside(c, t) and scale about 0.55 so cloud figures are at least 110 px tall; speech uses the new iconBalloon. Never place either over a face.
Set LIFE.t = t each frame for automatic blinks; give every character a gaze target in every scene (lookAt or gazePlan); stagger the two pals by 3 to 6 frames in every shared reaction.
The LATER card at 82.75 to 83.55 (caption BACK AT THE HOUSE...) hides the cut from the alley to the house: put the camera and set switch at its covered midpoint.

Effects only at the listed times (6.0, 20.8, 27.0, 62.9, 127.1, 146.95, 150.8, 168.6), all inside narration pauses, SND master 0.6. Knocks, stamps and thuds that fall on spoken words are visual only (lettering).
Panel-only shake for the missed grab at 112.9; captions never move.
The shroff holds the stick from 87.66 to 152.04 (right hand); when he walks to the door or the desk it hangs at his side, and during writing it lies across his lap.
warnings: The English translation is a condensed paraphrase of the Arabic (for example the laughing companions in P1 and the crowded streets in P7 are only in the Arabic); both are kept verbatim.
person is front-facing only: runs and walks read through leg cycle, tip and travel; over-shoulder looks are done with pupils and the look field.
Reaching the shelf depends on arm length (about 74 units at s 1): verify with stills and lower the shelf option if the hands do not meet the purse.
S8 and S11 are long dialogue scenes (20 s and 23 s): keep the listed icon and gesture changes on their words so something changes every 1 to 2 s.
If FIG.thief has only two variants, pal2 needs a colour override so the three thieves stay distinct.
The crowd must stay cheap: 9 figures, baked set behind, no per-figure gaze plans.
